responses:
The current program is a branch ladder that peels 16 words per recursive call and returns directly from each leaf for the tail. Its cost has been flat at 3567 across three attempts, so the remaining overhead is likely per-call and per-branch. The change below targets the per-call cost on large inputs. I can't measure the effect here, and the test-vector length distribution is unknown, so treat this as a hypothesis to validate with giri.

**Change 1: halve the recursion depth on the hot path.** Peeling 32 words per call instead of 16 halves the number of recursive calls, and their prologue and epilogue SSA instructions, for long inputs. Inputs of 16 to 31 words take the existing ladder path unchanged, so short-input behavior is untouched. The `xs[16:]` recursion covers the rest.

**Why this might help:** each recursive call costs a fixed prologue and epilogue on top of the 16 popcounts. Doubling the peel width roughly halves that overhead for long vectors. The cost is code length, which the feedback flagged, so the gain depends on whether the test vectors are long enough for the extra calls to matter. If they are mostly short (under 16 words), this change does nothing and only adds a dead branch. The next step would be to check the test-vector length distribution before committing to this.
